title: Flourishing of the Swahili Coast city-states
summary: Trading city-states along the East African coast, including Kilwa, flourished from about 1100 to about 1500, trading with African, Arabian, Persian, Indian and Chinese partners. Kilwa Kisiwani, occupied from the 9th to the 19th century, peaked in the 13th and 14th centuries on Indian Ocean trade in gold and ivory.

uncertainty.note: World History Encyclopedia timeline: c. 1100 - c. 1500, height from the 12th to 15th century; UNESCO: Kilwa peak in the 13th and 14th centuries.
